newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends mixed, switches active.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends mixed, switches active.

text.p: CSCE cocoa prices ended mixed on Monday, with focus centered on the spreads, as speculators continued to roll forward March positions ahead of the spot contract's first notice day on Friday.
"It was just a continuation of the rolling we saw last week," one trader said. "It was really a nothing day. There was a small range and most of the volume was done in switches."
Traders said speculative liquidation pressured the spot March contract, which fell $2 a tonne on the day, to $1,267, after ranging from $1,276 to $1,260.
Active second-month May closed up $2, to $1,303, posting traded from $1,310 to $1,291. The outer months finished $2 to $6 firmer.

Operators have steadily rolled March positions forward into May over the last several sessions, traders said. As of Friday, March open interest was down 1,812 lots from the previous session, to 13,257 lots, while May's open interest rose by 2,231 lots to 29,076 lots.

Technically, traders pegged near-term May support at $1,291, a double bottom on the charts and its life-of-contract low. The next downside target was seen at $1,280, while resistance was put near $1,235.
March support was pegged at $1,255, its life-of-contract low, and dealers said the spot contract would need to get above the $1,300 level to pick up any momentum.
On the fundamental side, traders said a pick-up in West African arrivals and a perception of plentiful supplies in the near-term is expected to continue to weigh on the market.
Volume Monday was moderate, at an estimated 8,710 lots.
